title: Theta-filtered merge candidates (all k)
switch: RBP_V3_THETA (default 1 in this commit; RBP_V3_LOOKUP default set to 0 here so the commit's default build is v3-2 = change 2 alone). RBP_V3_STATS (default 0) adds per-query candidate counts.
design: New per-launch device words: theta (uint32, 0 before every launch) and counts[range] (uint32 per range). The last block resets theta together with the done counter.

Rank pass (existing 4c rank computation): the key whose rank is k-1 (it exists exactly when the range has at least k documents) does atomicMax(theta, its score). Barrier; thread 0 reads theta into shared; barrier.

Write pass: keys with score >= theta recompute their rank and are written at that rank (the survivors are a prefix of the range's canonical order, so ranks 0..count-1 are filled). A shared counter gives count; thread 0 stores counts[range] and fences before taking the done ticket.

Merge (last block): thread 0 reads the final theta into shared; owned_best treats a list as ending at counts[l] and skips a head whose score is below theta (lists are descending, so nothing after it survives). Ordering unchanged: score descending, then original numeric ID ascending.
The empty-slot marking for ranges with fewer than k documents is replaced by counts.
safety_argument: A range whose k-th score is s has k documents with score >= s, so the global k-th score is >= s. Hence theta (a maximum of such s) never exceeds the global k-th score, at any time. Every global top-k document has score >= global k-th >= theta, is in its range's top-k list (canonical disjoint-partition argument), and is therefore written and survives the final filter. Equal scores are kept (>=), so ties at the cutoff are decided by original ID in the merge as before.
bugs_and_edge_cases_checked_in_design: Stale theta reads (other blocks raising it concurrently) only weaken the filter; any value read is <= the global k-th score.
Ranges with fewer than k documents never raise theta and write all their documents with score >= theta.
All scores zero: k-th scores are 0, theta stays 0, every candidate is kept; ties resolved by ID.
Fewer than k nonzero documents overall: zeros remain eligible because theta is 0 whenever some range's k-th score is 0.
k = 1: the range's best key raises theta to the global maximum observed so far.

Visibility: counts[range] and the candidate writes are fenced before the done ticket (all threads fence before S5; thread 0 fences again after writing the count), so the merging block reads complete lists; theta's atomicMax precedes the issuing block's fence and ticket.
The write pass recomputes ranks only for surviving keys, so the worst case (theta 0) costs one extra rank computation per key compared with V2-5; it never writes more than k candidates.
Barrier uniformity: the two new barriers are outside data-dependent branches.
semantics: Same canonical top-k; only the number of candidates written and merged changes.
risks: Two extra block barriers per range and a second rank computation for survivors may cost more than the merge saves at small k; measured by the gate's development readings and later on cuda5.
Early-finishing ranges see theta = 0 and write k candidates, so the saving depends on block scheduling order.
Parva's batched copy of range_scores and tests/check_batched_kernel_sync.py are not edited and will need a refresh.
tests: v3 theta cases (all-zero, few nonzero, ties at the k-th score across ranges, k above a range's size, k = 0, 1, 10, 128, 1000), the existing suite, and 100K/1M x 500 queries x k = 10/100/1000; RBP_V3_STATS build to confirm candidates written and survivors.

after_implementation.switch_off_identity: -DRBP_V3_THETA=0 (with RBP_V3_LOOKUP=0, this commit's default) compiles to SASS identical to ctrl (CUDA 13.3 34c94253cf61c499).
after_implementation.resources: 40 registers (unchanged), no spills, static shared 3,744 B (+16 B), ~6 blocks/SM estimate at k=10/100/1000.
after_implementation.statistics_build: RBP_V3_STATS=1, 1M, W=1024, first 25 calibration queries (laptop): candidates written per query median 477 / 4,435 / 334,272 at k=10/100/1000 against 9,770 / 97,700 / 977,000 for V2-5; survivors after the final filter median 44 / 684 / 74,029.
